attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Create one high-resolution character portrait-card fusion using exactly two inputs. Image1 is the original bear card, controlling the actual pose, upturned open mouth with limited visible teeth, real red neck-shoulder cloth, lighting, full frame, backing, note, and crop. Image2 controls the golden-yellow smooth compact round mascot identity and anatomy, including green-ringed black eyes. Transform the bear anatomy into the mascot anatomy; do not retain a human face or a bear snout. The original crown tuft is natural fur, not a cap, and must not be interpreted as human hairstyle, eyebrow hair, moustache, or beard. Preserve the exact original head roll/tilt and cheerful open-mouth expression. The very short broad natural neck joins the unclothed yellow upper body; do not invent a human collar, long shaft, or yellow throat funnel. Keep the actual red neck/shoulder ribbon/cloth visible at image-left. All solid surfaces must be opaque, with genuine alpha only outside the complete original card. Fine ambiguous details should be understated. Do not add extra figures, shirts, uniforms, neckties, or belly bibs. 
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: Original character is an unclothed BROWN BEAR, NOT A HUMAN: head tilted/upturned to IMAGE-RIGHT, mouth OPEN with limited visible teeth, rounded ears and a short natural fur tuft on crown. The tuft is FUR, NOT A CAP. Preserve exact original head roll/tilt, open-mouth expression and body pose while transforming BEAR ANATOMY into user golden-yellow compact round mascot anatomy with green-ringed black eyes. Bear fur is its body surface, not a human hairstyle/moustache; do not invent human hair, eyebrow hair, beard, glasses, cap, shirt, uniform, necktie or collar. Preserve actual RED neck/shoulder ribbon/cloth visible at IMAGE-LEFT and all original note/frame/backing. Very short broad natural neck joins unclothed yellow upper body; no human collar, long shaft, snout or yellow throat funnel. Reference mascot identity governs round face/ears/body; keep source pose and cheerful open-mouth character expression, no extra figures.
Only BEAR body anatomy becomes smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot identity, green-ringed black eyes, no bear snout or invented human hair/facial hair/clothes/collar. Keep actual head tilt toward image-right and open mouth with limited teeth, actual red cloth at image-left, very short broad natural neck directly joining unclothed yellow upper body. No neck shaft/funnel or cream neck bib. Preserve full original frame, opaque backing and note, no alpha holes in solid body/cloth. Image1 exact original card; Image2 user mascot identity/anatomy only. Fine ambiguous details stay understated, no invented symbols, readable text, labels, watermark, extra figures or comparison sheet.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
attempts.rejection_reason: Actually viewed original BEAR card, matched larger bear context (analysis only), full raw output, paired sheet and white/cyan/alpha panels. Correct smooth golden mascot animal identity, green eyes, open mouth, natural head tuft/ears, red neck/shoulder cloth, no human costume, and opaque backing/frame/note. Composition was changed from the primary close bear head/upper-chest crop into a standing figure with full torso, hanging hands and visible legs. Separate exact-master builtin composition repair: restore the primary large head/upper-chest scale and upward head pose, exclude newly revealed lower body/limbs, retain natural animal body and red cloth, add no human collar or facial hair. Cream lower body is mascot identity, not a clothing or alpha defect. Do not invent a roll-direction finding from this composition issue.
